Proof of Theorem 11.

For part (1), consider two manifested endpoints pp and qq. Endpoint pp has closed its local carrier after emitting token tt, and exports 𝖲𝖤𝖭𝖣⁡(t)∈Op\mathsf{SEND}(t)\in O_{p}. Before delivery, qq’s stable local inventory contains no carrier. Both endpoints can truthfully report that their local carrier sets are closed, yet tt can subsequently create a destination carrier if no terminal disposition or destination fence is required. The local statements alone are identical to a trace in which tt was rejected. The composite distinguishes the traces only by requiring a unique 𝖠𝖢𝖪⁡(t,d)\mathsf{ACK}(t,d) and, for acceptance, coverage of the resulting carrier. Equivalently, composition requires equality of the canonical token projections πt​(O​(E))\pi_{t}(O(E)) and πt​(B​(E))\pi_{t}(B(E)); it does not equate the differently typed send and acknowledgement records. Therefore local closure does not compose without token conservation.

For part (2), fix all visible evidence and consider an opaque reachable endpoint pp. In world w0w_{0}, pp has no residual root-dependent carrier. In world w1w_{1}, it has one delayed callback holding aca_{c} and able to commit a protected effect. By hypothesis, pp exposes neither an inventory capable of distinguishing these states nor a fence/frontier that eliminates the callback’s effect path. Every observation available to a verifier outside pp is therefore the same in w0w_{0} and w1w_{1}.

Any deterministic or randomized verifier receiving the same observation has the same output distribution in the two worlds. If it returns QQ, it is unsound in w1w_{1}; if it never returns QQ, it is incomplete in w0w_{0}. No observer of the remaining evidence is both sound and complete. Recording the missing endpoint as UU preserves soundness and identifies the exact evidence or enforcement capability needed to resolve the verdict. ∎

A.4. Preservation, algebra, and recovery

Proof of Theorem 12.

By premise, W′W^{\prime} is a registered sufficient witness, excludes aca_{c}, and is current. Definition 3 re-runs authorization under W′W^{\prime} and atomically installs it as the selected witness. The resulting carrier therefore has exercisable authority derived from every atom in W′W^{\prime}, not from aca_{c}. Retiring aca_{c} changes neither the epoch nor the grant digest of an atom in W′W^{\prime}, so the cut cannot invalidate that derivation.

The rebind receipt proves the support change to the leaf verifier, permitting the carrier to leave DcD_{c} without being terminated. The composite certificate names aca_{c} and is evaluated only against dependencies selected under that atom; it contains no transition revoking an atom in W′W^{\prime}. Thus the protocol removes exactly the retired root’s contribution while preserving independently supported work. A later change to an atom in W′W^{\prime} is handled by its own epoch transition and is outside this certificate’s effect. ∎

Proof of Theorem 13.

Fix compatibility header χ\chi. For each leaf identifier, the merge rule is the scalar operation

⊥⊔z=z,z⊔z=z,z⊔z′=𝖼𝗈𝗇𝖿𝗅𝗂𝖼𝗍(z≠z′),\bot\sqcup z=z,\qquad z\sqcup z=z,\qquad z\sqcup z^{\prime}=\mathsf{conflict}\quad(z\neq z^{\prime}),

with 𝖼𝗈𝗇𝖿𝗅𝗂𝖼𝗍⊔z=𝖼𝗈𝗇𝖿𝗅𝗂𝖼𝗍\mathsf{conflict}\sqcup z=\mathsf{conflict}. This is the join on a flat domain whose bottom is absence and whose top is authenticated conflict. Its case definition is associative, commutative, and idempotent. Finite pointwise products of such joins retain all three properties. Header disagreement maps to the same absorbing conflict element, so it does not change the argument.

The canonical composite serialization sorts leaf identifiers and token keys; therefore equal maps have equal composite digests independent of message arrival order. Definition 5 is a pure function of that map, its verified facts, and the frozen manifest. Duplicate delivery changes none of them. Different authenticated bodies under one leaf identifier remain at 𝖼𝗈𝗇𝖿𝗅𝗂𝖼𝗍\mathsf{conflict}, which triggers UU and cannot be overwritten by a later duplicate. The digest and verdict are consequently merge-order independent. ∎

Proof of Theorem 14.

Partition a crash around each security-changing transaction’s durable linearization point. Before the point, recovery observes no transition and a retry may execute normally. After the point, recovery observes the complete transition and the same idempotency key returns its committed result. A3 and A9 make epoch advances, cut records, fences, terminal carrier states, closed frontiers, and terminal token dispositions monotone. A retry proposing a different body under the same key is authenticated conflict, never a replacement.

An old grant request names retired epoch ee, so every later issuer transition fails after the cut advances rr to e+1e+1. A replayed carrier message is handled separately at its manifested endpoint: before the local barrier it remains an explicitly accounted transfer or acceptance, and after the barrier it is rejected. A replayed fence or close record is idempotent. A second token disposition violates the unique canonical token binding and becomes a conflict. A rebind receipt is bound to c​i​dcid, carrier id, old and new support digests, exact operation and effect-envelope digests, profile digest, and a single-use transition key; replay can neither rebind another carrier, widen its effect envelope, nor create a second accepted transition.

For certificate issuance, the authenticated certificate binds q​i​dqid and hqh_{q}, and the durable issuance record commits (c​i​d,q​i​d,hq,H⁡(E),sc,𝒞c)(cid,qid,h_{q},H(E),s_{c},\mathcal{C}_{c}), where hqh_{q} digests the canonical pre-certificate body. Repeating that exact identifier and candidate digest finds the durable record and returns the identical signature and certificate identity. Reusing q​i​dqid with a different body is an idempotency conflict; using another request identifier for the already completed c​i​dcid is a conflicting remint. A9 rejects both cases. Certificate replay therefore states the same historical fact and cannot upgrade different evidence or mint a second certificate for the generation.

For locality, let root identifier r′≠rr^{\prime}\neq r be absent from the frozen manifest dependencies and from rid⁡(W)\operatorname{rid}(W) for every selected witness WW represented by EE. Advancing r′r^{\prime}’s epoch or changing its ledger phase alters none of χ\chi, the leaf bodies, channel reconciliation, rebind receipts, or frontier facts on which Vc​(E)V_{c}(E) depends. The canonical projection used to verify 𝒞c\mathcal{C}_{c} is unchanged. Hence unrelated-root advancement cannot invalidate the root-relative certificate, while any shared selected witness would, by definition, make the root related and require fresh evidence. ∎

A.5. Conditional convergence

Proof of Theorem 15.

Lemma 7 prevents issuer-side creation or expansion of authority selected under aca_{c} after cc. A10 and fair execution install every manifested bp​(c)b_{p}(c); A5 then prevents further commitment admissions under aca_{c} at each sink. Pre-cut tokens delivered or accepted while barriers are propagating remain in DcD_{c} through their exact channel records rather than escaping the population. A11 directly supplies finiteness of the complete cut-dependent population of carriers, effects, and tokens, and ensures that each emitted token is eventually delivered to a covered destination or obtains an authenticated fence-reject or enforced-expiry disposition.

After the last required barrier is durable, consider the finite set of unresolved cut obligations. It contains one obligation for every dependent carrier not yet closed, terminal, 𝖯𝖱𝖤​_​𝖥𝖤𝖭𝖢𝖤​_​𝖢𝖮𝖬𝖬𝖨𝖳𝖳𝖤𝖣\mathsf{PRE\_FENCE\_COMMITTED}, or rebound; every token without a valid terminal disposition; every missing fence/frontier attestation; every transient pre-certification unknown or resolvable state disagreement; and every missing compatible leaf scope. Token acceptance transfers the same causal obligation from in transit to a covered destination carrier, so it does not remove the obligation from this set prematurely. Under A7, A10, A11, and the theorem premises, fair execution eventually discharges each member. Monotonicity prevents a discharged terminal fact from reopening, and A10 clears transient pre-certification unknowns and state disagreements. An authenticated same-key equivocation is absorbing for the generation and would permanently preclude QQ; the theorem’s no-equivocation premise excludes that case rather than treating it as clearable evidence.

The resulting compatible evidence covers every manifest scope and every provider frontier. Each acceptance in KcpK_{c}^{p} precedes its local barrier and has an exact typed receipt, every continuing carrier has an admissible state, and πt​(O⁡(E))=πt​(B⁡(E))\pi_{t}(O(E))=\pi_{t}(B(E)) with each acceptance linked to a covered carrier. A5 excludes an accepted post-barrier commitment, so there is no NN witness; A10 leaves no UU fact. Definition 5 returns QQ, and the verifier issues 𝒞c\mathcal{C}_{c}. Before all obligations discharge, a concrete open element produces NN or a missing, opaque, or conflicting fact produces UU; neither authorizes a certificate. ∎
